title: Shopify Plus Adobe Commerce Case Studies 2026: APAC Numbers
summary: Shopify Plus Adobe Commerce case studies 2026 analysed — MR DIY Malaysia and Pinalli benchmarks, real TCO maths, and where Adobe still wins in Asia-Pacific.
body_markdown:
The most useful thing about the Shopify Plus Adobe Commerce case studies 2026 crop — MR DIY Malaysia and Pinalli being the two most circulated — is not that Shopify won them. It is what the published numbers leave out. Both are retail-footprint businesses with heavy store networks, and both measured success in operational throughput rather than in a cost-of-ownership line item. If you are running a replatform evaluation from Hong Kong, Singapore, Sydney or Kuala Lumpur, that distinction decides whether the case study is evidence or marketing.


*Related reading:*[Salesforce AI Agent Seat Pricing Impact 2026: APAC Retail Math](https://branch8.com/posts/salesforce-ai-agent-seat-pricing-impact-2026-apac-retail)


I have sat on both sides of this. Vendor case studies are written to close deals, not to inform a CFO. They are still worth reading, provided you read them for mechanism rather than for the headline percentage.


## The 2026 case studies are retail-footprint stories, not technology stories


MR DIY is Malaysia's largest home improvement retailer, operating over 1,400 outlets across Malaysia according to the group's investor disclosures on Bursa Malaysia. Pinalli is an Italian prestige beauty chain with a few dozen stores and a strong clienteling model. Neither is a digital-native brand. Both moved to Shopify Plus from heavier stacks.


*Related reading:*[AI LLM Data Quality Ambiguity Resolution Beats Model Scale](https://branch8.com/posts/ai-llm-data-quality-ambiguity-resolution-apac)


That shared shape matters more than the platform logos. These are businesses where online is a minority of revenue but a majority of the operational complexity: store fulfilment, loyalty across channels, promotions that have to be identical at the till and on the PDP.


Adobe's own customer success library is weighted the other way — toward large manufacturers, B2B distributors and brands running complex multi-site catalogues under a single licence (business.adobe.com). When people search for "shopify plus adobe commerce case studies 2026 reddit" and find threads saying "pick the boring one," that is the real finding. The platform follows the operating model.


## Published case studies measure launch speed, almost never total cost of ownership


Shopify's enterprise comparison material claims Adobe Commerce implementation costs run roughly 42% higher than Shopify's on average, and that storefronts launch materially faster on Shopify (shopify.com). That is a vendor-funded statistic. It is directionally consistent with what I have seen in APAC builds, but it measures the wrong window — launch, not year three.


*Related reading:*[High Precision Diagnostic AI Clinical Trial: The APAC Data Edge](https://branch8.com/posts/high-precision-diagnostic-ai-clinical-trial-apac-data)


*Related reading:*[AI Contractor Security: Data Breach Risk Mitigation for APAC Teams](https://branch8.com/posts/ai-contractor-security-data-breach-risk-mitigation-apac)


Here is what the Pinalli and MR DIY write-ups do not publish: the previous licence cost, the hosting bill, the agency retainer before and after, and the headcount attached to patching. Without those four numbers, "reduced total cost of ownership" is an assertion.


The honest version of the cost comparison for a mid-size APAC enterprise:


- **Shopify Plus** lists from USD 2,300 per month on a three-year term, with hosting, PCI scope, CDN and platform upgrades included (shopify.com/plus). Variable platform fees on GMV above contracted thresholds are the line most finance teams miss.
- **Adobe Commerce** licences are quoted on GMV bands, typically starting in the low tens of thousands USD annually and rising steeply; Adobe does not publish rate cards (business.adobe.com). On top sits cloud infrastructure, a managed services partner, and upgrade projects every few minor releases.


The cross-over point in our modelling work usually sits where catalogue complexity — not revenue — crosses a threshold. A HKD 300M online business with 4,000 simple SKUs is cheaper on Shopify Plus. A smaller business with configurable industrial products, contract pricing per dealer and three ERPs is frequently cheaper on Adobe Commerce, because the alternative is buying your way out with apps and middleware.

## Shopify's growth rate is the strongest signal in the dataset


Ignore case studies for a moment and look at platform momentum, because that determines app availability, partner depth and hiring pool in Asia-Pacific five years out.


Shopify reported revenue growth in the low-to-mid 30s percent year over year through 2025, with quarterly GMV in the high tens of billions USD (investors.shopify.com). Adobe's Digital Experience segment — which contains Commerce alongside Analytics, Target and AEM — has grown roughly 10–11% annually (Adobe investor relations). Commerce is a minority of that segment.


BuiltWith's platform trend data shows Magento/Adobe Commerce live site counts in long-term decline since the Magento 1 end-of-life in June 2020, while Shopify's installed base continues to climb (trends.builtwith.com). That is not a verdict on engineering quality. It is a statement about where the talent and the third-party integrations will be in 2029.


For APAC specifically, this compounds. eMarketer data consistently puts Asia-Pacific above half of global retail e-commerce sales. Yet the regional partner market for Adobe Commerce is thin outside Australia, Japan and India — if your Magento team sits in a single Vietnamese or Philippine agency, your platform risk is concentration risk.


## MR DIY's win was throughput, and that is a specific technical claim


A 1,400-store retailer with low average order value does not replatform for a prettier PDP. It replatforms because the previous stack could not absorb promotional traffic, store pickup volumes and catalogue churn without engineering intervention.


The measurable version of that claim is checkout and admin throughput. Shopify's platform-managed checkout removes the single largest source of custom code in a Magento build — and the single largest source of conversion loss. Baymard Institute's aggregated research puts the documented average cart abandonment rate at 70.19% across 49 studies (baymard.com). Every point recovered there is worth more than most merchandising projects.


If you are evaluating, test checkout under your own conditions. Shopify's checkout extensibility model replaced` checkout.liquid` customisation with Functions and UI extensions, which means your customisations survive upgrades instead of blocking them:

That is the shape of enterprise logic on Shopify Plus in 2026: sandboxed, versioned, and not in the upgrade path. On Adobe Commerce the equivalent lives in a module that someone has to regression-test every release.

## Pinalli shows the clienteling gap has effectively closed


The historical argument for keeping a beauty or jewellery retailer on Adobe Commerce was customer data depth — segmentation, tiered loyalty, store-associate tooling. Pinalli's move indicates that argument has weakened for European and Asian specialty retail alike.


Shopify's published figures for Pinalli cite growth in online performance and operational simplification after leaving a heavier stack. What the case study does not disclose is the pre-migration baseline or the app subscription stack required post-migration. Treat the growth figure as an upper bound on the platform's contribution, because replatforms are almost always bundled with a redesign, a new email programme and fresh paid spend. Attribution across those is rarely clean.


We have run the same pattern with a Hong Kong multi-brand catering group and with a Greater China specialty retailer: the platform change is maybe a third of the lift. The merchandising discipline forced by the migration is the rest.


## Adobe Commerce still wins in four specific APAC scenarios


I am not going to pretend the answer is always Shopify. Adobe Commerce remains the better call when:


- **Configurable or made-to-order products** drive revenue — bundles with dependent options, CPQ-style pricing, engineered goods. Shopify's variant model has improved but still imposes structural limits.
- **Dealer and distributor networks** need per-account catalogues, credit terms and negotiated pricing at scale. B2B on Shopify has closed much of this gap since 2023; it has not closed all of it.
- **Data residency or on-premise hosting** is contractually required — common for state-linked enterprises in mainland China, Indonesia and parts of the Gulf. Adobe Commerce can be self-hosted; Shopify cannot.
- **You already own the Adobe stack** — AEM, Analytics, Real-Time CDP. The integration economics change when Commerce is the fourth product on an existing enterprise agreement.


If none of those four apply to you, the Reddit consensus is correct and you are spending money to preserve optionality you will never use.

## Benchmarks to hold any 2026 case study against


When a vendor or agency hands you a PDF, check it against these. Most published Shopify Plus Adobe Commerce case studies 2026 will fail at least three:


1. **Baseline disclosed?** Pre-migration revenue, conversion rate and page speed, not just the after.
2. **Observation window stated?** Under six months post-launch is noise.
3. **Confounders named?** Redesign, new paid budget, new markets, seasonality.
4. **TCO over 36 months?** Licence plus hosting plus apps plus agency plus internal headcount.
5. **App stack listed?** Shopify Plus TCO is often 20–40% app subscriptions by month 18, in our modelling.
6. **Migration duration and failure points?** Any build that claims zero rollback is editing history.
7. **Who paid for the study?** Both vendors fund theirs.


## What APAC teams get wrong in the evaluation


Three recurring errors.


First, pricing the licence instead of the operating model. The expensive part of Adobe Commerce is rarely the licence — it is the standing engineering capacity required to keep it current. If you cannot staff two competent PHP engineers in your market, the platform is unaffordable at any licence price.


Second, underweighting payments and local checkout. In Southeast Asia, your conversion depends on GrabPay, FPX, PayNow, DuitNow, ShopeePay, QRIS and instalment providers. Check coverage with actual acquirers in each market before you decide — this differs materially between Malaysia, Indonesia and Taiwan.


Third, ignoring the ERP seam. Whether you run SAP, NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics or a local Hong Kong ERP, inventory and order sync is where projects slip. Specify the integration contract first, platform second.

## What to do Monday morning


1. **Build the 36-month TCO sheet before you book a vendor demo.** Licence, hosting, apps, agency retainer, internal headcount, payment processing delta. Model Shopify Plus variable GMV fees against Adobe's licence bands at your projected three-year revenue — not today's.
2. **Audit your custom code against the four Adobe-wins scenarios.** List every Magento module you maintain. For each, note whether it maps to a Shopify Function, an app, or nothing. The "nothing" column is your real migration cost.
3. **Request the baseline data behind any case study you were sent.** If the partner cannot produce pre-migration conversion and page-speed figures under NDA, score the study as marketing and move on.
